messages:
anya: FYI I rolled the kernel-threshold change at 08:10 and short-chat p95 on host nodes spiked immediately (65ms -> 135ms). Dashboard: https://perf.redwood/q/587654

dave: thanks. is this confined to a region or across all canaries?

anya: seen in canaries + hosted-eu. Quick flame: host-ingress/tokenize ~42%, stream-assembler flush ~20%, kernel-dispatch overhead ~18%, kvcache miss handling ~12%.

tia: tokenize jump is odd. any recent proto or http2 tweaks?

anya: we also switched to micro-framing for grpc to reduce tail for large seqs. micro-frames appear to trigger a copy-path in the ingress when fragments < 256B. Logs show repeated "proto-copy-fallback" on small frames.

ops-bot: deploys: kernel-threshold=v2 rolled to canary @5876543210 by anya

dave: another angle: the new kernel selection seems to prefer 'fused-attn' for >64 tokens which changes batching behavior for short requests. Could modify how requests coalesce into kvcache groups.

anya: kvcache stats: short-key miss rate pre-rollout 3.7% -> 14.8% post-rollout. Backend tail increased too.

tia: that matches hypothesis: batching/clustering change -> different key distribution -> more misses -> backend latency amplifies text gen tail.

dave: plan: 1) rollback kernel-threshold on canary 2) run A/B disabling micro-frame preference 3) add ingress metric: writev_count vs copy_count 4) compute kvcache_group_entropy metric to quantify fragmentation

anya: rolling rollback now. starting a trace capture for both paths.

perf-bot: regression-detect: short_text_p95 +102% (canary) — traces linked

tia: small test idea: harness that runs many 32-64 token requests and asserts zero-copy writev used for fragments to avoid per-frag memcpy. If writev fallback triggers, fail.

dave: good. i'll add the harness to ingress-ci and also a kvcache coalescing unit that simulates batching boundaries.

anya: rollback applied. early signal: p95 back to ~72ms in canary. writev vs copy ratio reverted to previous levels.

ops-bot: rollback completed on canary @5876543215

anya: conclusion: the kernel-threshold tweak indirectly changed batching windows which interacted with new micro-framing -> forced proto-copy path and fragmented kvcache groups. Dominant cost was host ingress copy + increased backend misses.

tia: follow-ups: - make micro-framing opt-in for canary until we validate ingress zero-copy path - add ingress telemetry (writev/copy) PERF-2021 - add kvcache_group_entropy alert PERF-2022 - revert hold-window change from threshold patch or tune threshold to preserve old coalescing

dave: added tickets: PERF-2021, PERF-2022, PERF-2023. I'll own tuning the kernel thresholds.

anya: thanks all. keeping the thread open until canary finishes a 30m sweep.

perf-bot: update: canary sweep completed @5876543222 — regressions resolved after rollback.
